assessment_summary:
Attempting to prove the statement step by step:
1. The statement claims that Quicksort runs in O(n log n) time on every input.
2. By the provided definitions, we are evaluating the deterministic textbook version of Quicksort that always chooses the first element as the pivot and uses Lomuto partition, with running time measured by the number of key comparisons.
3. Consider an already-sorted array of size n as input.
4. The chosen pivot (the first element) is the minimum element of the subarray. 
5. The partitioning step compares this pivot to the other n-1 elements. Because it is the minimum, the partition is maximally unbalanced, leaving an empty left subarray and a right subarray of size n-1.
6. The recursive call on the right subarray of size n-1, which is also sorted, will again use its first element as the pivot, requiring n-2 comparisons, and so on.
7. The total number of key comparisons is (n-1) + (n-2) + ... + 1 = n(n-1)/2, which is O(n^2), not O(n log n).

Because the very first claim of the statement (that Quicksort runs in O(n log n) time on every input) is false under these definitions, the proof attempt fails immediately. Moreover, the second claim that an already-sorted array is a cheap case is also false as it is the worst case for comparisons.
flawed_step: Quicksort runs in O(n log n) time on every input
